title: At someone's home
goal: Visit a friend's family and feel at ease: arrive and ask what's done in their home, accept and refuse food the polite way, offer to help, stay the night and say goodbye, and talk about how things used to be.
intro:
Sooner or later a friend will say *come over, my mum's making dinner*. Indian hospitality is warm and generous, and it has its own little script: the guest says no, the host insists, the guest gives in and has 'just a little'. Knowing the lines makes you a guest everyone wants back.

In this unit you'll learn what to say at the door, at the table, in the kitchen and when you stay over. The grammar gives you **'used to'** (बचपन में हम यहाँ आते थे), the language of **offering and declining**, and the quick **'shall I…?'** questions (जूते उतारूँ? बर्तन धो दूँ?) that a good guest keeps asking.

grammar.title: 'Used to': रहता था and जाया करते थे
grammar.body:
To say what you **used to** do — habits and repeated actions in the past — take the habitual form you know from the present (**-ता / -ती / -ते**) and put **था / थी / थे** after it instead of है:

मैं यहाँ **रहता था** — I used to live here (man)
वह चाय नहीं **पीती थी** — she didn't use to drink tea
हम हर रविवार क्रिकेट **खेलते थे** — we used to play cricket every Sunday

The ending agrees with the subject, and there is **no ने**, even with verbs like खाना, पीना, देखना: मैं रोज़ दूध **पीता था**, never मैंने.

For a fixed, regular habit — often with a nostalgic feel — Hindi also has **past form + करना**: हम हर गर्मी नानी के घर **जाया करते थे** 'we used to go to Gran's every summer'. Note that जाना becomes **जाया** here. Both forms mean the same; -ता था is the everyday one.

The classic contrast is **पहले … आजकल / अब …** 'before … these days / now …'.

**Don't mix up:** **खाता था** 'used to eat' · **खा रहा था** 'was eating (at that moment)' · **खाया था** 'had eaten / ate (once)'.

grammar.title: Offering, insisting and saying no politely
grammar.body:
Hospitality in Hindi has a rhythm: **offer → polite refusal → insisting → accepting a little**. Refusing the first offer is good manners, and a good host never takes the first 'no' seriously.

**Offering:**
• polite imperative + **ना** to make it warm: **लीजिए ना**, **लो ना** 'do have some'
• the future as a gentle question: **चाय लेंगे?** 'will you have tea?'
• **और** 'more': **और लीजिए** 'have some more', **एक और** 'one more'
• 'shall I…?' with the subjunctive: **पानी लाऊँ?**

**Declining softly:**
• **नहीं-नहीं, बस!** 'no, no, that's enough!'
• **रहने दीजिए / रहने दो** 'leave it, don't bother'
• **मैं अभी खाकर आया हूँ** 'I've just eaten'
• **तकल्लुफ़ मत कीजिए** 'please don't go to any trouble'

**Accepting:** **अच्छा, बस थोड़ा सा** 'OK, just a little'.

Hosts insist (**ज़िद करना**) with **शर्माओ मत** 'don't be shy' and **अपना ही घर समझो**. And instead of saying 'thank you' again and again, which can sound distant, **praise the food**: खाना बहुत अच्छा बना है!

examples.en: Will you have tea or a cold drink?

examples.native: नहीं-नहीं, रहने दीजिए, मैं अभी खाकर आया हूँ।
examples.roman: nahīṃ-nahīṃ, rahne dījiye, maiṃ abhī khākar āyā hūṃ.
examples.en: No, no, please don't, I've just eaten. (man)

examples.native: अरे, शर्माओ मत, अपना ही घर है।
examples.roman: are, sharmāo mat, apnā hī ghar hai.
examples.en: Hey, don't be shy, it's your home too.

examples.roman: achchhā, āp itnī zid kar rahī haiṃ to thoṛā sā.
examples.en: Well, since you insist, just a little.

grammar.title: Shall I…? The subjunctive with दूँ and लूँ
grammar.body:
A good guest keeps checking: *shall I take my shoes off? can I sit here? shall I help?* Hindi asks all of these with the **subjunctive** (unit 18), which for मैं ends in **-ऊँ**:

उतारना → **उतारूँ?** 'shall I take (them) off?'
बैठना → **बैठूँ?** 'shall I sit?'
करना → **करूँ?** 'shall I do?'

To **offer to do something for someone**, add **दूँ** (from देना 'give') to the stem: **मैं बर्तन धो दूँ?** 'shall I wash the dishes (for you)?', **झाड़ू लगा दूँ?** 'shall I sweep?'. To ask to **take or do something for yourself**, use **लूँ** (from लेना): **मैं पानी ले लूँ?** 'can I get myself some water?'.

For **advice** — 'should I, is it the custom?' — use **चाहिए**: **क्या मुझे कुछ लाना चाहिए?** 'should I bring something?'. For **permission**, use **सकना**: **क्या मैं यहाँ फ़ोन चार्ज कर सकता हूँ?**

To let someone do something, use the oblique infinitive + **देना**: **मुझे करने दीजिए** 'let me do it', **उसे खाने दो** 'let him eat'.

examples.en: Shall I leave my shoes right here?
Can I come into the kitchen?

examples.native: प्लीज़, मुझे भी कुछ करने दीजिए।
examples.roman: plīz, mujhe bhī kuchh karne dījiye.
examples.en: Please, let me do something too.

dialogue.title: Dinner at Rohit's
dialogue.setting: Sam has been invited to dinner at his friend Rohit's family home in Jaipur. Rohit's mum has cooked.

lines.en: Oh, it's nothing, Aunty. Rohit said you love ghevar.

lines.speaker: Aunty
lines.native: अरे वाह! चलो, बैठो, खाना तैयार है। शर्माना मत, अपना ही घर समझो।

lines.speaker: Aunty
lines.native: रोहित के नाना जी भी यही करते थे। "बस-बस" बोलते थे, और फिर दो रोटी और खाते थे!

lines.native: हा हा! अच्छा आंटी, मैं बर्तन धो दूँ?

lines.native: और इतनी रात को कहाँ जाओगे? आज यहीं रुक जाओ, मेरे कमरे में बहुत जगह है।

lines.en: Sure? It won't be any trouble for Aunty?

lines.roman: kaisī taklīf? maiṃ abhī chādar aur takiyā le ātī hūṃ.
lines.en: What trouble? I'll get you a sheet and a pillow right now.

culture: Call your friend's parents **आंटी** and **अंकल** (add **जी** for extra respect), never by their first names; in traditional families younger people touch elders' feet in greeting, but a warm **नमस्ते** with folded hands is always fine for a guest. Take your shoes off at the door unless told not to, and never wear them into the kitchen or the **पूजा** corner. Don't arrive empty-handed: a box of sweets (**मिठाई**) or fruit is the classic gift; don't bring alcohol unless you know the family drinks. At the table, expect the offer–refuse–insist routine: hosts keep refilling your plate (in Rajasthan this insisting has its own name, **मनुहार**), so leave a little food if you're truly full, and say **बस** firmly with a hand over the plate. Offer to help clear up — you'll usually be refused, but carrying your own plate to the kitchen is appreciated. Staying over is normal and hosts mean the offer. When you leave, the family often walks you to the door or gate and asks you to text when you get home (**पहुँचकर मैसेज कर देना**).

tip.title: Shall I…? — उतारूँ? बैठूँ?
tip.body:
- 'Shall I…?' uses the subjunctive: मैं → **-ऊँ**: **उतारूँ? बैठूँ? आऊँ?**
- To offer to do it (for someone), add **दूँ**: उतार **दूँ**? For yourself, **लूँ**: पानी ले **लूँ**?
- Advice, 'should I?': **क्या मुझे … चाहिए?**
tip.pattern: मैं + stem + ऊँ? · stem + दूँ / लूँ?

lessons.title: At the table: yes, no and "just a little"

tip.title: Offer, refuse, insist, accept
tip.body:
- Offer warmly with **ना**: **लीजिए ना**, **लो ना**; or ask with the future: चाय **लेंगे**?
- Refuse softly first: **नहीं-नहीं, बस!** · **रहने दीजिए**.
- The host insists (**ज़िद करना**): शर्माओ मत! Then accept: **बस, थोड़ा सा**.
- Thank the cook by praising the food: खाना बहुत अच्छा **बना** है!
tip.pattern: offer (लीजिए ना) → बस! → ज़िद → थोड़ा सा

tip.title: Used to: करता था
tip.body:
- Habitual form + **था / थी / थे**: मैं यहाँ **रहता था** 'I used to live here', वह **पीती थी** 'she used to drink'.
- No **ने**, even with खाना, पीना, देखना.
- For a regular habit you also hear **past form + करना**: हम वहाँ **जाया करते थे**.
- Contrast: **पहले** … **आजकल** … 'before … these days …'.

sentences.en: Didn't you use to live here?

sentences.native: पापा रात को खाने के बाद ख़बरें देखा करते थे।
sentences.roman: pāpā rāt ko khāne ke bād xabareṃ dekhā karte the.
sentences.en: Dad used to watch the news after dinner.

sentences.native: मुझे जल्दी उठने की आदत नहीं है।
sentences.roman: mujhe jaldī uṭhne kī ādat nahīṃ hai.
sentences.en: I'm not used to getting up early.

sentences.native: आंटी की मेहमाननवाज़ी का जवाब नहीं!
sentences.roman: āṇṭī kī mehmānnavāzī kā javāb nahīṃ!
sentences.en: Aunty's hospitality is second to none!

tip.title: Shall I do it? Let me do it!
tip.body:
- Offer: **मैं बर्तन धो दूँ?** · **मैं कुछ मदद करूँ?**
- The host will say **रहने दो / रहने दीजिए** 'leave it'.
- Insist with oblique infinitive + **देना** 'let': **मुझे करने दीजिए** 'let me do it'.
- Accepting help: **अच्छा, ठीक है, धो दो**.

sentences.native: मैं बर्तन धो दूँ?
sentences.roman: maiṃ bartan dho dūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I do the dishes?

sentences.native: नहीं-नहीं, रहने दो, तुम मेहमान हो।
sentences.roman: nahīṃ-nahīṃ, rahne do, tum mehmān ho.
sentences.en: No, no, leave it, you're a guest.

sentences.native: प्लीज़ आंटी, मुझे करने दीजिए।
sentences.roman: plīz āṇṭī, mujhe karne dījiye.
sentences.en: Please, Aunty, let me do it.

sentences.native: मुझे भी कुछ करने दो ना!
sentences.roman: mujhe bhī kuchh karne do nā!
sentences.en: Let me do something too!

sentences.native: हमारे घर में सब अपने बर्तन ख़ुद धोते हैं।
sentences.roman: hamāre ghar meṃ sab apne bartan xud dhote haiṃ.
sentences.en: In our house everyone washes their own dishes.

sentences.native: रविवार को हम सब मिलकर सफ़ाई करते हैं।
sentences.roman: ravivār ko ham sab milkar safāī karte haiṃ.
sentences.en: On Sundays we all clean together.

sentences.native: मैं झाड़ू लगा दूँ?
sentences.roman: maiṃ jhāṛū lagā dūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I sweep?

sentences.native: मैं मेज़ साफ़ कर दूँ?
sentences.roman: maiṃ mez sāf kar dūṃ?
sentences.en: Shall I wipe the table?

sentences.native: अरे, रहने दीजिए, मैं ख़ुद कर लूँगी।
sentences.roman: are, rahne dījiye, maiṃ xud kar lūṃgī.
sentences.en: Oh, leave it, I'll do it myself. (woman)

sentences.native: आंटी, मैं रसोई में कुछ मदद करूँ?
sentences.roman: āṇṭī, maiṃ rasoī meṃ kuchh madad karūṃ?
sentences.en: Aunty, can I help with anything in the kitchen?

tip.title: हमारे यहाँ — at our place
tip.body:
- **X के यहाँ** = at X's place: **हमारे यहाँ** ठहरो 'stay at ours', पार्टी **राहुल के यहाँ** है.
- Inviting someone to stay: **यहीं रुक जाओ** (friend) · **यहीं रुक जाइए** (polite).
- **रुकना** and **ठहरना** both mean 'stay'; रुकना is more everyday.

sentences.native: आज रात हमारे यहाँ ठहरो, बहुत देर हो गई है।
sentences.roman: āj rāt hamāre yahāṃ ṭhaharo, bahut der ho gaī hai.
sentences.en: Stay at ours tonight, it's got really late.

sentences.native: आज पार्टी राहुल के यहाँ है।
sentences.roman: āj pārṭī Rāhul ke yahāṃ hai.
sentences.en: Tonight's party is at Rahul's.

sentences.native: हमारे पास बहुत जगह है, कोई तकलीफ़ नहीं।
sentences.roman: hamāre pās bahut jagah hai, koī taklīf nahīṃ.
sentences.en: We've got plenty of room, it's no trouble.

sentences.native: मैं सोफ़े पर सो जाऊँगा।
sentences.roman: maiṃ sofe par so jāūṃgā.
sentences.en: I'll sleep on the sofa. (man)

sentences.native: एक और तकिया मिलेगा?
sentences.roman: ek aur takiyā milegā?
sentences.en: Could I have another pillow?

sentences.native: रात को ठंड होती है, कंबल ले लो।
sentences.roman: rāt ko ṭhaṇḍ hotī hai, kambal le lo.
sentences.en: It gets cold at night, take a blanket.

sentences.native: मैं तुम्हारे लिए गद्दा बिछा देती हूँ।
sentences.roman: maiṃ tumhāre liye gaddā bichhā detī hūṃ.
sentences.en: I'll put a mattress down for you. (woman)

sentences.native: चादर अलमारी में है।
sentences.roman: chādar almārī meṃ hai.
sentences.en: The sheets are in the cupboard.

sentences.native: पक्का? तुम्हारे घरवालों को तकलीफ़ तो नहीं होगी?
sentences.roman: pakkā? tumhāre gharvāloṃ ko taklīf to nahīṃ hogī?
sentences.en: Sure? It won't be a problem for your family?

sentences.native: आप भी आज यहीं रुक जाइए, अंकल।
sentences.roman: āp bhī āj yahīṃ ruk jāiye, aṅkal.
sentences.en: You stay here tonight too, Uncle.

sentences.native: अच्छा आंटी, अब मुझे चलना चाहिए, बहुत देर हो गई।
sentences.roman: achchhā āṇṭī, ab mujhe chalnā chāhiye, bahut der ho gaī.
sentences.en: Right, Aunty, I should get going, it's late.

sentences.native: अरे, इतनी जल्दी? खाना खाकर जाओ।
sentences.roman: are, itnī jaldī? khānā khākar jāo.
sentences.en: What, so soon? Stay and eat first.

sentences.native: नहीं आंटी, घर पर सब इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं।
sentences.roman: nahīṃ āṇṭī, ghar par sab intazār kar rahe haiṃ.
sentences.en: No, Aunty, everyone's waiting for me at home.

sentences.native: बेटा, फिर आना, और घरवालों को नमस्ते कहना।
sentences.roman: beṭā, phir ānā, aur gharvāloṃ ko namaste kahnā.
sentences.en: Come again, dear, and say hello to your family.

sentences.native: कोई भी ज़रूरत हो तो बेझिझक बताना।
sentences.roman: koī bhī zarūrat ho to bejhijhak batānā.
sentences.en: If you need anything at all, don't hesitate to ask.

sentences.native: पहुँचकर मैसेज कर देना, ठीक है?
sentences.roman: pahuṃchkar maisej kar denā, ṭhīk hai?
sentences.en: Text me when you get home, OK?

sentences.native: बहुत मज़ा आया, आंटी, खाना भी बहुत अच्छा था।
sentences.roman: bahut mazā āyā, āṇṭī, khānā bhī bahut achchhā thā.
sentences.en: I had a great time, Aunty, and the food was lovely.

sentences.native: अगली बार आप लोग हमारे यहाँ आइए।
sentences.roman: aglī bār āp log hamāre yahāṃ āiye.
sentences.en: Next time you all come to ours.

sentences.native: पहले हम हर हफ़्ते मिलते थे, अब बहुत कम मिलते हैं।
sentences.roman: pahle ham har hafte milte the, ab bahut kam milte haiṃ.
sentences.en: We used to meet every week; now we hardly ever do.
